title: Impressionism
examples: What is the difference between Impressionism and Realism?
How did technology affect Impressionist painting?
Can you show me an example of light in Impressionism?

explain.say: Today we are learning about Impressionism in art history. This style focused on capturing the fleeting moment. Artists were very interested in how light changed things.
The Impressionists paid close attention to how light affected colour. They used broken colour to show bright effects. Think about sunlight hitting water.
Another key technique was painting outdoors, which is called plein air. This allowed them to capture changing natural light. They left the studio for the subject.
Impressionist paintings often depicted everyday modern life. They painted scenes of ordinary people and leisure activities. These subjects were new to art.
In real life, imagine watching people at a busy outdoor market. The way the sunlight hits the fruit and the people changes every minute. That is what they tried to capture.
A common mistake is thinking they painted nothing important. They actually captured a very specific vision of the moment. The subject was the light itself.

faq.q: Were Impressionists the first to paint outside?
faq.a: No, painting outdoors had been done before. However, the Impressionists were the first to make it a central subject matter. They treated the outdoors as a primary source of artistic study.
asks: Did they invent plein air painting?
Was painting outside new to them?

faq.q: Did they paint things that were only important to rich people?
faq.a: No, they deliberately moved away from grand historical or mythological scenes. They focused on the lives of the middle class and everyday people. This was a big change in art history.
asks: Did they only paint rich people?
What did they choose to paint instead?

faq.q: Why do their paintings look a bit blurry sometimes?
faq.a: That blurriness comes from their technique of using visible, quick brushstrokes. They wanted to capture the quick change of light, not perfect detail. This technique is what gives the style its name.
asks: What is the name for those quick strokes?

faq.q: Did they use bright colours only?
faq.a: They used bright colours because they were trying to mimic the intensity of natural light. They often placed complementary colours next to each other to make them vibrate optically. This creates a vivid effect.
asks: How did they make colours pop?

faq.q: Did they paint famous historical battles?
faq.a: No, that was more typical of earlier academic art. They preferred scenes of modern leisure, like picnics or boating trips. They celebrated the modern, everyday experience.
asks: What kind of scenes did they prefer?

facts: Impressionism focused on capturing the changing effects of natural light.
Plein air means painting outdoors, a major development for the style.
They used visible, distinct brushstrokes rather than smooth blending.
Subjects included modern life, such as city scenes and leisure activities.

quiz.say: Which technique did Impressionists use to show bright colour effects?

options.show: Mixing pure colours on the canvas
options.say: Mixing pure colours on the canvas

quiz.why: Mixing pure colours on the canvas makes the colours appear brighter when viewed from a distance.

wrong.0: Outlines restrict the natural flow and changing quality of the light.
wrong.1: This prevents them from capturing the specific light found outdoors.
wrong.3: This creates a duller, more blended colour that loses the vibrancy of light.

quiz.say: If an artist painted a busy train station, what modern life aspect are they capturing?
quiz.why: Train stations and boulevards were symbols of the rapidly changing, modern urban world.

wrong.0: They moved away from depicting only the powerful elite.
wrong.2: This was a subject from earlier art periods, not the focus here.
wrong.3: While they painted nature, the focus was on the urban, modern experience.

quiz.say: When painting outdoors, what did the Impressionists try to capture most?
quiz.why: The entire goal was to record the way light changed the appearance of a scene at a specific instant.

wrong.0: If they painted perfect detail, they would lose the sense of the passing moment.
wrong.1: They were more interested in the surface appearance than the underlying form.
wrong.2: Their focus was on the visual experience, not telling a grand story.
